statement: Such diagram factorization is unlikely in general without the base TC--F factorization.
notes: Heuristic motivation, not an impossibility theorem; for I=e it is exactly the base problem.

statement: Proposition3.7: factorization of ((TC)<I>,F(I)) suffices for C<I>∩W(I)=(TC)<I>.
gap_or_error: The proof leaves implicit why an objectwise F-map in W is objectwise TF.
repair: Complete the implicit lemma by a pushout along C, a Cof_3 factorization, and a lift against TC; then use the source's retract proof. This fills an explanation, not a false premise.

statement: In the proof, p in F(I)∩W(I) belongs to TF(I).
repair: For p:X→Y in F∩W and a square from a:A→B in C, form Z=X⊔_A B, factor Z→Y as ℓ in C followed by q in W, and lift p against ℓj in TC. The resulting composite B→Z→T→X is the desired lift.
notes: Neither a second factorization nor retract closure of W is needed for this inclusion.

statement: The coherent lift q shows f is a retract of i in the arrow category.
repair: The section and retraction are (1_X,q) and (1_X,p), with pq=1_Y and qf=i.
notes: Printed prose calls the new diagonal p; diagram and identities correctly name it q.

statement: (TC)<I> is retract closed, so the retract f belongs to it.
repair: Every left lifting class is closed under retracts.

statement: Corollary3.8: a closed Quillen triple with TC Q-special satisfies the identity for every small I.
repair: Apply the diagram small object theorem to TC and then Proposition3.7; C need not itself have a small generating family for this equality.

statement: The equality of3.8 did not require C to be Q-special.
repair: The proof used only the other diagram factorization, besides the existing base cofibration axioms.

statement: The author's available construction of general projective factorizations still needs C Q-special.
notes: Statement of the author's method and uncertainty, not a theorem that every model category is cofibrantly generated.

statement: Question3.9 requests a closed Quillen structure whose prederivator lacks some u!^W.
repair: Example3.11 works for the historical finite-completeness convention. Under modern bicompleteness, arbitrary model categories give derivators and no such example exists.

statement: Question3.9 also requests such a structure lacking some u*^W.
repair: The same bounded F_2-complex example fails on the right; bicomplete model categories have the right Kan extensions by the cited theorem.

statement: The author presumes testing u:I→e should suffice for general Kan extensions.
repair: Pointwise comma-category formulas establish this strategy in derivator constructions; adjoints to terminal projections alone do not supply those formulas for an arbitrary prederivator.
notes: Do not record an unproved general implication as formal.

statement: The requested counterexample would be stronger with cocomplete accessible ambient M and L-accessible W.
repair: For an arbitrary localizer, the finite Boolean example developed after3.14 meets all these explicit size/continuity conditions; it admits no compatible Cof_4 structure.
notes: The model-structure version remains excluded by the bicomplete model theorem.

statement: The group category BG is suggested as a shape beyond noetherian posets.
repair: Example3.11 realizes the suggestion for C_2; its nerve has arbitrarily long composable strings despite being a finite category.

statement: Example3.10: (all maps,isomorphisms) is a closed Quillen factorization pair in any category.
repair: Factor f as f then identity; a map with RLP against all maps lifts against itself and is invertible.

statement: Example3.10: (isomorphisms,all maps) is a closed Quillen factorization pair in any category.
repair: Factor f as identity then f; the dual self-lifting argument identifies the left class.

statement: With finite limits and colimits, W=Iso and C=F=all maps is a closed Quillen triple.
repair: Both lifting pairs and both factorizations have just been verified; keep the source's footnote about finite existence.

statement: For every I, W(I)=Iso(M(I)) and Ho_W(I)=M(I).
repair: A natural transformation is invertible iff all its components are; localization at isomorphisms is an equivalence.

statement: For Example3.10 homotopy Kan-extension existence is exactly ordinary Kan-extension existence.
repair: Restriction functors agree under the preceding equivalences, so their adjoints agree.

statement: For u:I→e in Example3.10, the left adjoint exists iff all I^op-colimits exist in M.
repair: The left adjoint to the constant-diagram functor is precisely the colimit functor.

statement: For u:I→e in Example3.10, the right adjoint exists iff all I^op-limits exist in M.
repair: Dual universal property.

statement: For a functor between finite categories both ordinary Kan extensions exist under finite completeness and cocompleteness.
repair: Their comma categories are finite, so the pointwise ordinary Kan formulas use only the available finite limits and colimits.

statement: Example3.11 defines M=K^b(k-Ab) as bounded cochain complexes and W as quasi-isomorphisms.
notes: The source's K^b denotes actual complexes here, not the modern homotopy-category notation; write C^b in commentary to avoid ambiguity.

statement: Localization of that category at quasi-isomorphisms is D^b(k-Ab).
repair: This is the defining bounded derived category; chain-homotopy equivalent maps are already identified by localization.

statement: Enough projectives should supply a closed Quillen structure on bounded complexes, perhaps requiring finite cohomological dimension of k.
gap_or_error: The cited bounded-above construction cannot simply be restricted using enough projectives alone; bounded replacements may fail.
repair: For the author's chosen field F_2 give a complete finite Quillen structure: C=degreewise injections,F=degreewise surjections,W=quasi-isomorphisms. Cone constructions give both bounded factorizations and contractible disks give both liftings.
notes: The author explicitly voices the qualification. No claim of a counterexample to every possible bounded model structure over a general ring is made.

statement: For I=BG, M(I) is the category of bounded complexes of k[G]-modules.
repair: BG has a single object, so its diagram has one bound; compatible group actions are exactly module structures.
notes: This identification would need a uniform-boundedness restriction for general infinitely many-object I.

statement: The left adjoint exists iff the derived coinvariants of every bounded complex remain bounded.
repair: The unbounded derived adjunction restricts when bounded; conversely test a hypothetical bounded left adjoint against shifts of an injective cogenerator to detect all derived-tensor homology.

statement: The right adjoint exists iff the derived invariants of every bounded complex remain bounded.
repair: Restrict the usual derived adjunction for sufficiency; shifts of k detect cohomology of any proposed right adjoint and give necessity.

statement: It suffices to test modules concentrated in one degree for either boundedness condition.
repair: A bounded complex has a finite truncation filtration by its cohomology modules; an exact derived functor preserves its finite triangles. Bounds may depend on the module.

statement: Left boundedness is equivalent to eventual vanishing of H_i(G,M), for every module M.
repair: These are the homology groups of the derived coinvariant complex.

statement: Right boundedness is equivalent to eventual vanishing of H^i(G,M), for every module M.
repair: These are the cohomology groups of the derived invariant complex.

statement: For k=Z and finite G, those vanishing conditions hold for all modules only when G is trivial.
repair: For nontrivial finite G choose C_p≤G and induce its trivial F_p-module; finite-index induction equals coinduction. The cyclic periodic resolution and Shapiro give nonzero groups in arbitrarily high degrees in both theories.

statement: The economical counterexample is G=C_2 and k=F_2.
repair: For A=F_2[epsilon]/epsilon², the repeated-epsilon resolution gives Tor_n^A(k,k)=Ext_A^n(k,k)=k for all n≥0. Complete adjunction nonexistence proof in commentary.

statement: For that example both u!^W and u*^W fail although I is a finite category.
repair: A hypothetical right adjoint has cohomology k in every nonnegative degree; a left adjoint has nonzero maps to k[n] for every n. Both contradict boundedness.

statement: The bounded-complex ambient category does not admit all small colimits.
repair: A coproduct of shifts k[n] would contain each as a retract and hence have nonzero cohomology in infinitely many degrees.

statement: Example3.12 assumes a strongly saturated localization R:M→H with fully faithful left adjoint L.
notes: This is a coreflective inclusion L, not a reflective inclusion in the opposite adjunction direction.

statement: In that situation W=R^{-1}(Iso(H)).
repair: Strong saturation is exactly this property for the localization functor.

statement: For every small I, Ho_W(I)≃H(I).
repair: The unit of L^I⊣R^I is invertible and the counit is objectwise in W; after localization they give inverse equivalences.

statement: If M has all small limits, then H has them.
repair: For D:J→H, R lim_M LD represents its limit by the adjunction.

statement: A counterexample might have bicomplete M but H lack some small colimits.
repair: Impossible in this adjunction setup: for X=colim_M LD the counit LRX→X is invertible. The proof factors the cocone uniquely through the counit and verifies both inverse identities. Hence the full image of L is automatically closed under all small colimits.
notes: The source proposes a route and voices difficulty; the formal obstruction is proved in the commentary.

statement: A small cogenerating family in M induces one in H.
repair: If {C_s} conservatively detects arrows, then {RC_s} does so since Hom_H(-,RC_s)=Hom_M(L-,C_s) and L reflects isomorphisms.

statement: Completeness plus a small cogenerating family gives colimits in H by SGA4 I8.12.7.
notes: The exact conservative-generator convention and representability criterion were checked. This sufficient argument is redundant for the coreflective setup because colimit closure is automatic.

statement: Colimits exist if H is identified with a full subcategory of M closed under small colimits.
repair: In the situation actually under discussion, that closure follows from coreflectivity, not from an extra assumption.

statement: Question3.13: can a locally U-small category have all U-small colimits but lack some U-small limits?
repair: Yes: the poset Ord_U of U-small ordinals has suprema of all U-small families and initial object0 but no terminal object. The category is U-large.

statement: Such a category has no small generating family.
repair: Correct for the conservative represented-Hom convention of SGA4 I7.1. In Ord_U any small generator candidate is bounded by beta, so beta→beta+1 induces bijections on all those Hom-sets but is not invertible.
notes: A merely faithful family would not have this implication in a poset; do not substitute that weaker modern convention.

statement: In particular such a category cannot be equivalent to a small category.
repair: A small category has a small conservative generating family consisting of all its objects; the stated completeness criterion applies.

statement: Question3.14: a cofibration category satisfying Cof_4 should have u!^W for all small u.
repair: True. Cof_4 supplies the coproduct and sequential-colimit ABC axioms; Radulescu-Banu Theorem10.3.2 gives strong left derivability. Cisinski Corollary6.21 gives the dual equivalent formulation.
notes: Modern proof settles the statement, not the validity of Anderson's proof as criticized in the manuscript.

statement: The author requests a localizer on bicomplete M whose prederivator lacks some left or right Kan extension, perhaps with M small.
repair: Explicit finite counterexample: P=P({1,2,3}), W identities plus {1}→{1,2}. Its localization is a seven-object poset lacking join({2},{3}) and meet({1,3},{2,3}); both adjoints for discrete2→e fail. Complete normal-form proof supplied as a modest commentators development.

statement: The author is less convinced such a counterexample exists when W is filtered-colimit stable and M has accessible objects and a cardinal filtration.
repair: The same finite Boolean example meets every explicit qualification. Filtered diagrams in a finite poset have a maximum value in their image; all objects are finitely presentable, W is closed under filtered colimits and is a finite accessible full arrow subcategory.
notes: The unspecified possible extra conditions are not a definite proposition. No compatible Cof_4 structure is claimed.

statement: Question3.15 asks whether an L-accessible arrow class in the stated accessible complete ambient category has a small left Q-generating subset.
repair: Negative even in the locally finitely presentable category of directed multigraphs: pure monomorphisms supply a counterexample. Full-arrow aleph1-accessibility and arbitrary filtered-colimit closure are proved explicitly in the commentary.
notes: No additional set-theoretic principle is needed for this counterexample; source proof_status records its historical question.

statement: Question3.15 allows the extra assumption that Φ is left Q-saturated: isomorphisms, cobase change, composition, and retracts.
repair: The pure-monomorphism counterexample satisfies these closures and even transfinite closure. Cox et al. Theorem5.1 excludes cofibrant generation because the parallel-pair indexing category is not locally linearly preordered. A small Q-generating subset would imply cofibrant generation by the small object argument, contradiction.
notes: Q-saturated is the actual wording; do not replace it with the stronger Q-closed hypothesis.

statement: The listed closure operations are equivalent to the local Q-saturation notion being invoked.
notes: Transfinite closure follows additionally in the L-accessible setting from filtered-colimit stability together with finite composition; the source distinguishes this from Q-closedness.

statement: The author requests any mutually Q-orthogonal closed pair that does not factor all arrows.
repair: On the rational poset, fix irrational r. Left maps are identities or arrows ending below r; right maps are identities or arrows beginning above r. They are mutual lifting orthogonals, but any arrow crossing r has no such factorization. Complete proof in commentary.
notes: Taylor Example5.7.10 is cited for an established nonfactorization phenomenon in a poset, not for this exact rational-cut presentation.

statement: The same nonfactorization request with special ambient M is of particular interest.
gap_or_error: The rational-cut example is not cocomplete and therefore does not answer this stronger variant.
repair: Keep this variant explicitly separate; neither the pure-monomorphism result nor the finite-localizer result automatically supplies a nonfactorizing mutually closed pair in a special category.
notes: The commentary does not claim present-day openness merely from not locating a definitive answer.

statement: The chapter ends by proposing a systematic study of factorization between lifting classes.
notes: Research programme rather than an additional theorem.
